_comment: MYCIN-2026 OFFLINE board-exam bank — FREE-TEXT (prose) items. Unlike items.json (already-structured relation/subject/var), these are prose stems as a board exam poses them. The offline pipeline (board_offline.py) decomposes each stem into an ADJ recall query with a LOCAL in-memory model, then the NATIVE adj-lang engine answers over the grounded edges — zero ONLINE model calls (enforced by offline_guard.no_network). Each item carries the gold ANSWER and the gold QUERY: cache-mode uses the gold query (proving the engine+plumbing+guard deterministically, offline, in CI); --model mode runs the local model and scores its decomposition against the gold query AND the end-to-end answer. 'gold' ABSTAIN = a deliberately-uncovered entity the engine must decline rather than fabricate.

items.stem: A 6-month-old infant of Ashkenazi Jewish descent has progressive developmental regression, an exaggerated startle response to sound, and a cherry-red spot on the macula. Tay-Sachs disease is diagnosed. Which enzyme is deficient?

An adult presents with hepatosplenomegaly, bone pain, pancytopenia, and lipid-laden macrophages with a 'crumpled tissue paper' cytoplasm on marrow biopsy, consistent with Gaucher disease. Which enzyme is deficient?
A neonate not on newborn screening develops intellectual disability, eczema, a musty body odor, and fair skin. Classic phenylketonuria is diagnosed. Which enzyme is deficient?
A floppy infant has marked hypotonia, a markedly enlarged heart, and macroglossia, with glycogen accumulation in lysosomes. Pompe disease is diagnosed. Which enzyme is deficient?

An infant has severe fasting hypoglycemia, a protuberant abdomen from massive hepatomegaly, lactic acidosis, and hyperuricemia. Von Gierke disease (glycogen storage disease type I) is diagnosed. Which enzyme is deficient?

A young man has episodic burning pain in the hands and feet, clusters of dark red angiokeratomas over the trunk, and proteinuria, with an X-linked family history. Fabry disease is diagnosed. Which enzyme is deficient?
In Tay-Sachs disease, which substrate accumulates in neurons because the degradative enzyme is missing?
A boy has severe self-mutilating lip and finger biting, choreoathetosis, hyperuricemia, and gout, due to HGPRT deficiency (Lesch-Nyhan syndrome). What is its inheritance pattern?

A patient with chronic alcohol use and poor intake develops high-output heart failure with peripheral edema and a sensorimotor polyneuropathy. Which disease does this thiamine (vitamin B1) deficiency cause?
A patient on an isoniazid-heavy regimen with a corn-based diet develops a photosensitive dermatitis, diarrhea, and dementia. Which disease does this niacin (vitamin B3) deficiency cause?

A patient with a diet devoid of fresh fruits and vegetables develops perifollicular hemorrhages, corkscrew hairs, swollen bleeding gums, and poor wound healing. Which disease does this vitamin C deficiency cause?
A toddler with little sun exposure has bowed legs, a rachitic rosary at the costochondral junctions, and delayed fontanelle closure. Which disease does this vitamin D deficiency cause?

A patient with pernicious anemia develops symmetric loss of vibration and proprioception with an ataxic gait from dorsal-column and lateral-corticospinal-tract degeneration. What is the classic neurologic finding of this cobalamin (vitamin B12) deficiency?
A menstruating woman has fatigue, pica, and koilonychia; labs show low ferritin and a low mean corpuscular volume. For iron deficiency anemia, what MCV class is this?
An elderly vegan has fatigue and glossitis with hypersegmented neutrophils on smear. For this vitamin B12 deficiency anemia, what MCV class is expected?

A patient of Northern European descent has jaundice, splenomegaly, gallstones, and a positive osmotic fragility test from a red-cell membrane protein defect (hereditary spherocytosis). What is the classic peripheral-smear finding?
A man develops acute hemolysis after eating fava beans or starting an oxidant drug, with Heinz bodies on supravital stain. For G6PD deficiency, what bite-removed cell is the classic smear finding?
Insulin lowers blood glucose by promoting cellular uptake. Which gland/cells secrete it?
Cortisol is the principal glucocorticoid of the stress response. Which gland/tissue secretes it?
A patient has fatigue, cold intolerance, weight gain, constipation, and delayed relaxation of reflexes from inadequate thyroxine. What is the named deficiency syndrome?

After pituitary surgery a patient passes large volumes of dilute urine with rising serum sodium and intense thirst, from a deficiency of antidiuretic hormone (ADH). What is the named deficiency syndrome?
A boy has hemarthroses and deep-tissue bleeding with a prolonged aPTT that corrects on mixing, and an X-linked inheritance (hemophilia A). Which clotting factor is deficient?

A patient has easy mucocutaneous bruising, heavy menses, and a prolonged bleeding time with the most common inherited bleeding disorder, von Willebrand disease. Which factor/protein is deficient or defective?
Hemophilia A predominantly affects males through carrier mothers. What is its inheritance pattern?
In hemophilia A, which coagulation screening test is prolonged while the PT stays normal?
A young adult has a movement disorder, Kayser-Fleischer rings, and hepatitis from copper accumulation (Wilson disease). Which enzyme is deficient?
Glucagon raises blood glucose during fasting. What is the named clinical syndrome of glucagon deficiency?
